takeaway: Mirizzi syndrome: a gallstone in the gallbladder compresses the common bile duct, causing obstructive jaundice, often with cholecystitis.

question.text: A 45-year-old woman has epigastric pain, jaundice, vomiting and fever. Ultrasound: gallstones, gallbladder wall 5 mm, common bile duct 9 mm, prominent intrahepatic ducts. Diagnosis?
question.say: A forty-five-year-old woman has epigastric pain, jaundice, vomiting and fever. Ultrasound shows gallstones, a gallbladder wall of five millimetres, a common bile duct of nine millimetres, and prominent intrahepatic ducts. What is the likely diagnosis?

lines.text: A gallbladder full of gallstones, with a thick wall.
lines.say: Look at the gallbladder, full of gallstones. The ultrasound also shows a gallbladder wall of five millimetres.

lines.text: One stone squeezes the common bile duct from outside.
lines.say: One stone is squeezing the common bile duct from outside. That is the Mirizzi squeeze.

lines.text: Above the squeeze the duct is dilated: 9 mm, with prominent ducts.
lines.say: Above the squeeze the duct is dilated, nine millimetres, and the intrahepatic ducts are prominent.

lines.text: The patient has obstructive jaundice, fever and pain.
lines.say: (sigh) The poor patient has obstructive jaundice, with fever, vomiting and epigastric pain.

lines.text: There is gallstone cholecystitis here as well.
lines.say: There is gallstone cholecystitis here as well.

lines.text: Remember: a gallstone compressing the common bile duct is Mirizzi syndrome.
lines.say: Remember: a gallstone compressing the common bile duct is Mirizzi syndrome.
